notes: 2026-09-22 fix round, working the impact/effort priority list agreed with the user against the independent critic's full findings. Quick wins so far, none of these scores updated yet — pending the critic's own re-verification, per this project's own division of labor (fixer proposes, critic re-scores independently): (1) ui toolbar 'null' text — fixed at the exact root cause the critic diagnosed (toolbar.js line ~141 used the native Element.append(), which stringifies a null argument, instead of this project's own null-filtering append() helper from dom.js); verified via the same DOM-level eval readback the critic used (pill.innerHTML no longer contains 'null'). (2) ui happiness-panel contradiction — animals/index.js's getHappiness(id) returned 0 (a valid number) for any id unknown to the module, silently overriding a correct fallback value; now returns null for an unknown id so callers can tell 'unknown to me' apart from 'genuinely 0% happy', matching the get()/getState() pattern already used elsewhere in the same file. Verified: the panel preset now shows 68% Content consistent with its own need bars, not 0% Miserable. (3) zoning boardwalk staircase — MAX_PULL (max smoothing displacement from the exact crack position) raised 2.0m -> 3.2m; confirmed by direct calculation this cannot cause the 'leak into a neighbouring region' failure the clamp exists to prevent, since even the thinnest corridor a player can paint (ZoneTool.js's own minimum brush radius is 4m, matching zoning/showcase.js's boardwalk demo exactly) leaves >=4m of clearance between two edges pulling the new full amount toward each other. Honest caveat: my own attempt at a rigorous visual/geometric re-verification of this one was inconclusive (couldn't reliably isolate the boardwalk's own boundary loop from the ribbon's combined vertex buffer via eval, and a custom close-up camera aim came back black) — the reasoning for the fix is sound and the change is low-risk, but treat this one as 'fixed, not independently confirmed by me' until the critic re-checks it directly.

2026-09-22 SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION found by the independent critic pass and fixed same day: the 2026-09-21 waterhole-black-patch fix (terrain/water.js's in-column-scatter floor, `outgoingLight += diffuseColor.rgb * 0.45`) was a flat linear-HDR addition applied BEFORE renderer.toneMappingExposure, so it scaled with whatever exposure the scene was using. At night the exposure ceiling is 12 (vs 4 by day — see environment's own history), and the water's other light terms are already small at night, so this floor became the dominant term and blew every water body to a uniform near-white glow, brighter than the park's own lamps. The independent critic caught this in six separate contexts (terrain, animals, traffic, savannah, park module reviews, and the game's own round-5 blind pass — game.blindVisual dropped 7.8 -> 6.8 almost entirely on the strength of one shot, `game-overview-21.5`) before I had looked at a single night-time water shot after making that fix myself. Root-caused and fixed by dividing the floor by the live exposure (a new `uExposure` uniform, updated per-frame from `renderer.toneMappingExposure`) so its DISPLAY brightness stays roughly constant across day and night instead of tracking the night ceiling. Verified: night-water-fix-verify.png (game overview 21.5h) now shows dark water with a soft warm rim, lamps correctly the brightest objects in frame again; sav-waterhole-fix-recheck.png confirms the original black-patch fix still holds (dappled shade, not a hard black hole). 89/89 tests pass, lint clean. The terrain/animals/traffic/savannah/park/game scores in this file still reflect the critic's pre-fix reads and have NOT been restored by me — re-scoring is the critic's job, not mine, to keep the pass independent; flagging this fix clearly for the next critic round to re-verify rather than assuming it fully resolves those modules' scores (several also cited unrelated issues).

FOURTH AND DEEPEST ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-05: environment/atmosphere.js lightDepth() reused scatter()'s view-density scratch array _d, so every CPU-sampled sky radiance came out ~10^4x too dim (measured zenith 7e-6 vs physical ~0.5). The exposure controller, reading a near-black sky, climbed to its ceiling; the visible 'sky' was the blown-out cloud deck; fog and aerial-perspective colours near black produced the horizon band. This is the true root cause of the round-1 SYSTEMIC 'washed out toward white' blocker and of both of environment's round-2 majors — NOT ACES tone mapping, NOT albedo authoring. The GPU LUT was unaffected (GLSL locals), which is why sun colour was always right while sky/fog colours were wrong. Fixed with a separate scratch array; wave-3 verification then proceeded against a correctly-lit world.

Wave 3 (savannah, park) verified 2026-09-05: both modules were already fully implemented in the ZIP but had never been screenshotted, scored, or documented (STATUS said 'not-started' — stale). All 17 savannah presets and 7 park presets + 9 full-game sweeps shot and READ; 0 console errors everywhere; all inside the draw/triangle budgets. savannah README written; park README's two placeholder sections filled with measured numbers; missing READMEs written for environment, simulation, ui, audio; traffic's 1-line draft replaced.

Screenshot-tooling note for future rounds: park's own setSpeed(1) used to push every capture into a random night hour under SwiftShader (~35 game-hours burn during the 40-frame settle at ~1 fps) — capture pages must pass &speed=0, and modules that advance the clock must respect an explicitly paused clock. Also: do not run 3+ concurrent SwiftShader renders on a 12-core machine — module imports starve and pages time out.
Egress proxy blocks Poly Haven / ambientCG / all CDNs: every asset is procedural.
Screenshot tool renders through SwiftShader (software GL); fps in shots/*.json is NOT a GPU number. Draw calls, triangles and errors are real.

Integration verified: all 15 modules load together in the full game with zero console errors, 278 draw calls, 4.74 M triangles (park's demo auto-builds on core:ready).

SECOND ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: environment/index.js clamped auto-exposure at 60x, and it was hitting 5.46x at golden hour / 60x at night on ordinary, correctly-lit scenes (Math.max(0, keyDir.y) kills the key-light term well before the sky actually looks dim as the sun nears the horizon). Every material several-fold overexposed, verified by reading a baked lion albedo texture directly (correct ~0.38 linear) against near-white on screen. Lowered the ceiling to 4 (commit e3a6999); night is now dim and legible with visible stars instead of blown to white, golden hour shows correct value separation between light/dark test objects instead of clipping everything. Needs a further tuning pass against real references but is no longer broken. This, independently of the sRGB double-encode, explains why several modules' screenshots looked washed out at low sun angles even after the sRGB fix — e.g. buildings' lodge preset (tod 17.5) flat-white background buildings.

THIRD ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: terrain/mesh.js had `mesh.receiveShadow = false; // BENCH`, a leftover benchmarking flag that silently blocked every shadow in the game from landing on the ground, anywhere. Fixed (commit e3a6999). This was the real cause of animals' round-1 'no contact shadow' blocker — animals had already shipped a drawn contact-shadow decal as a workaround, which stays in place as a complement now that real shadows also work.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-02: core/Textures.js gpu() double-encoded sRGB (shader-side linearToSRGBv plus an sRGB-internal-format render target). Linear 0.216 was stored as byte 188 instead of 128 — every albedo ~37% too bright. This, not ACES tone mapping, was the real cause of the project-wide washed-out look; the earlier 'author darker to compensate' guidance was a workaround over a core defect and is now WRONG. Core is fixed. Modules that compensated must have that compensation REMOVED: props is currently over-dark (near-black foliage), and any darkening added to animals/terrain/roads in round 2 must be re-checked.

issues.text: Asphalt macro-texture reads as a swirled/brushed pattern (sand-blasted concrete or fabric weave) rather than fine aggregate speckle -- visible at paved, junction, and an extra close-in angle, not a distance artifact.
sampleEdge(edgeId, s, out) allocates only when out is falsy and throws on a plain {x,z}-shaped object -- honestly documented but a real API sharp edge for traffic.
Showcase network uses fixed control-point coordinates rather than deriving from terrain.getFeatures() -- works today via dynamic bridge retargeting but is seed-fragile in principle (disclosed).

roads.good: Timber bridge is the standout asset -- correct deck, railings, arch, clean water integration. Dirt two-track at close range is convincing (ruts, dust-blended shoulders, no visible mesh boundary). Night lighting is the best-executed night scene of any module reviewed so far (self-contained reflective paint + lamp glow). Junction blending shows no z-fighting. Own-module budget independently verified via stats() (9 drawables, 44,753 triangles for a 12-edge network) comfortably inside the <=40 draws / <=200k triangle spec. API matches README, dispose() thorough.

issues.text: Toolbar active-tool pill renders a literal "null" as visible text (confirmed via innerHTML dump: "Building.Placenull...."). Root cause: pill.append(...) uses the native Element.append(), which stringifies a null child, instead of the project's own append() helper in dom.js which skips null/undefined. Fires in the module's own toolbar showcase preset.

Side panel can show "0% HAPPY / Miserable" contradicted by healthy need bars (83/50/52/65/77%) and "Doing fine" advice text. Root cause: animals.getHappiness(id) returns a hard 0 fallback for any id unknown to the real animals module registry -- exactly what happens for mock/showcase-injected animals (ui/mock.js writes directly into world.animals, bypassing animals.spawn()). The selected animal is also entirely absent from the 3D view for the same reason. Fires in the module's own panel showcase preset.

update()'s 0.5s refresh accumulator is wall-clock based, not frame-count based -- plausibly fires every frame under SwiftShader's slow frame time instead of twice a second, inflating measured updateMs (7.4-9.7ms EMA vs the 1.5ms/module budget); likely a measurement artifact of software GL rather than a confirmed real-hardware violation, but worth a frame-time-independent cap.
Empty notification panel container can appear; population/cash graph panel is a stub vs spec -- both already disclosed in the README.

ui.good: Visual/layout quality genuinely close to the Cities: Skylines II reference across overview/report/close/night. Daily report modal (canvas sparklines, income/expense breakdown, satisfaction rings, species table) is a complete, well-composed implementation. close preset shows the same panel system working correctly, proving the panel bug is a specific data-path defect not a systemic failure. Night HUD legibility excellent. Zero console errors anywhere; API matches README; dispose() thorough.

issues.text: bust preset staff panel shows some roles still over-staffed relative to "needed" despite bankruptcy -- plausible (no auto-firing, player must act) but reads oddly unexplained next to the BANKRUPT stamp.
Village modelled as a staff-morale/prosperity scalar, not a physical village layer -- disclosed simplification vs SimSafari 1998.
Visitors are aggregate counts/satisfaction, not individual agents -- disclosed, reasonable for a headless module.

simulation.good: Only module with real automated regression tests -- 89/89 passing, run directly by the critic (not taken on faith), including a determinism check and staged-population-reconciliation tests pinning the exact class of bug (silently-zeroed herd) the project has been burned by elsewhere. bust preset is a genuinely well-executed bankruptcy failure state (real stamp, visitor flatline, red happiness bars). Habitat-quality matrix (close preset) is a clear, correctly-thresholded implementation of the core spec requirement. Zero console errors across every preset; module-owned draw calls are 2; update()/tick() minimal and allocation-clean. Every claim independently checked held up.

issues.text: The module's own verification tool src/modules/audio/shot.mjs is broken: page.screenshot() hits the default 30s timeout on the first preset, reproduced twice. Root cause: same rAF-compositor-busy issue the core tools/screenshot.mjs was specifically hardened against (extended timeout/retry) -- shot.mjs never got that fix. Worked around via tools/screenshot.mjs --dom --gesture --eval instead, which confirmed the underlying audio engine is fine.

vehicles/animals buses read -inf dB in a still capture between scheduled sounds -- disclosed capture-timing artifact, consistent with what was observed (the event log shows real triggers even while the instantaneous meter reads -inf).
Synth calls are impressionistic, not species-accurate transcriptions -- disclosed, unavoidable without reference recordings.

audio.good: Debug panel is genuinely informative: live bus meters, populated 40Hz-16kHz spectrum, per-layer ambience gains, event log with real positions/distances. selfTest() covers the full 30-sound catalogue with plausible differentiated levels, no silent entries. Distance falloff measured directly (lion@10m -23.3dB vs @400m -46.9dB). Night/storm layer mixes matched the README's specific historical numbers closely, independently reproduced. dispose() genuinely closes the AudioContext and tears down every voice/engine loop.

issues.text: overview establishing shot reads visually flat against the AAA reference bar -- the effect is deliberately subtle (confirmed by the numbers), best appreciated at close range or via the off A/B, not on its own.
Ambient dust/smoke particles are only faintly visible even at close range (one rim-lit wisp) -- confirmed active via stats() (117 spawned) but easy to miss visually without the API readout.

effects.good: Every quantitative README claim reproduced exactly under independent verification: pipeline measure() returns exactly 12/12 extra draw calls (spec ceiling), matching triangle counts per preset, haze strength 0.875 (active, non-zero) at the heat preset, grade parameters (bloom 0.18, grain 0.02) within spec ceilings. GTAO contact shadows genuinely convincing at close range. Night bloom well-tuned (soft lamp halos, not blown out). Module's own draw-call attribution analysis (pipeline vs showcase-yard vs CSM cascade cost) is rigorous and correct. dispose() restores direct rendering and cleans up fully; update() allocation-free.

issues.text: Boundary-smoothing pipeline's headline claim ("never as the 4m cell staircase") is directly contradicted by the visitor-zone boardwalk path, which renders as an unmistakable right-angle staircase at the exact grid pitch in four separate screenshots across three times of day. Habitat-region boundaries elsewhere in the same frames do show genuine Chaikin/Taubin rounding, so this specifically affects narrow 1-2-cell-wide corridors, plausibly an edge case where the Taubin filter has no teeth left to melt without erasing the path.

updateMs (0.9-4.1ms) exceeds the general 1.5ms/module budget in 3 of 4 presets -- plausibly a SwiftShader wall-clock-cadence artifact (rebuildHabitats' 1.2s throttle firing every real frame), but rebuildHabitats is genuinely non-trivial work and deserves a frame-count-based throttle instead.

zoning.good: Habitat-region fill and boundary rendering (away from the boardwalk case) is genuinely good -- correct tinting, soft feathered edges, organic region shapes. Fence detail at close range is convincing and terrain-conforming. Own-module draw-call budget (4, vs <=20 spec ceiling) exact and confirmed. Zero console errors across every preset. API matches README; dispose() clean.

issues.text: Polish is uneven across the 16-type catalogue -- lodge and gate are clear hero assets, tower/hide-adjacent/staff-house structures read plainer at overview distance.

buildings.good: Thatch roof system (course lips, noise-displaced ragged eave, rolled ridge) genuinely convincing and matches the detailed README description exactly. Gate park-name sign legible and correct. Night lighting (lantern glow on thatch underside, warm deck pool) atmospheric, one of the better night results in the project. Own-module budget independently verified via stats() (34 draws, 131,730 triangles, 25 buildings/16 types) comfortably inside the <=60 draws / <=400k triangle spec. Zero console errors across every preset. API matches README; dispose() present and thorough.

issues.text: update() cost is 90x-175x over the 1.5ms budget on every single preset measured (132.5-262.8ms), not an occasional worst case. README discloses a 792ms grass-rebuild worst case but frames it as rare ("not every frame") -- in fact every preset switch IS a 14m threshold crossing, so this expensive rebuild fires on every preset load, every time. In the live game this is a repeated stutter on every camera pan/jump that crosses a chunk boundary.
kopje preset framed wide enough that the escarpment dominates the shot; could not clearly confirm "thorn scrub in the cracks" on the kopje itself at this framing.

props.good: Draw-call and triangle numbers match the README's own measurements exactly for every preset -- the most precise README-to-reproduction correspondence of any module reviewed. overview and riverine are the strongest single images reviewed in the project (naturalistic density gradients, correct silhouettes, atmospheric lighting). acacia and close demonstrate individual species/prop silhouettes precisely matching descriptions. Instancing delivers: 125-155 draws for 150k+ grass instances, comfortably inside the <=400 spec ceiling. API matches README; dispose() releases every instanced mesh; lint clean.

issues.text: overview preset (430m camera) makes vehicles nearly invisible -- disclosed honestly in the README as a presentation flaw, and independently confirmed to be exactly as significant as claimed (6 vehicles per stats(), genuinely present but unreadable at this distance).
Ambient vehicles never sight-stop (only tours do); passengers are static with no boarding animation -- both disclosed, consistent with what was observed.

traffic.good: Safari truck at close range is one of the better individual assets in the project (tiered bench seating, individually coloured passengers, canopy, roof rack, spare wheel). Sighting behaviour real and demonstrated. Night headlights and reflective road paint both convincing. Own-module budget independently confirmed via stats() (18 draws for 6 vehicles, well inside <=80-for-10 spec) and updateMs (0.66-0.70ms, well inside 2ms budget). API matches README; dispose() thorough.

issues.text: terrain preset measured 143.7ms for tools' own update() -- wildly out of line with every other preset (0.04-0.94ms). TerrainTool.js's update() has nothing that should cost this much (only a ring-cursor decal position update); tools has no dependency on props (which has a separate, confirmed severe grass-rebuild stall), so this could not be attributed with confidence. Flagged for a second look, not scored as confirmed.

close preset selection marker not visually legible in the captured screenshot despite genuinely existing (world.selection correctly set to {kind:building,id:b_1}, visible marker child confirmed via direct scene-graph eval check) -- a presentation/contrast issue at this camera angle/time, not a functional defect.

tools.good: Building ghost preview red/green validity colouring is unambiguous and precise. Terrain ring cursor cleanly conforms to terrain exactly where the scripted stroke says. Road preview ribbon correctly snaps onto the existing committed road (real graph-aware snapping). Night atmosphere (lodge glow, river moonlight reflection, reflective road paint) genuinely strong. dispose() releases ring/ribbon/marker/group; API matches README's documented tool framework.

issues.text: close preset shows the wrong scene -- a zebra/wildebeest herd crossing, near-identical in subject to the herd preset next to it -- instead of the described quiet foreground-grass-and-acacia-trunk-with-hazy-kopje composition. Confirmed via capture JSON that the correct preset and its own authored camera were used; no kopje visible at all in this shot.

hero flagship shot does not deliver its promised composition: roughly half the frame blown out by sun glare, no legible kopje silhouette on the right third (escarpment instead), no grazing herd visible in the middle distance.

Night waterhole glows uniformly bright (single brightest object in frame) -- same terrain/environment water-at-night bug independently confirmed in terrain, animals, traffic reviews this round; fourth cross-module data point.

savannah.good: overview, waterhole, kopje, herd, river, storm, and dawn all deliver exactly what their descriptions promise -- genuinely strong, well-composed, atmospheric photography-adjacent framing. kopje subject (lion pride) holds up under fresh independent inspection. river and dawn are among the best single images reviewed in this whole critic pass. Module adds no scene content of its own (verified via draw-call attribution); dispose()/API/lint clean.

issues.text: habitat preset shows an entirely different scene than its description -- a river/gallery view instead of the plains-grazer habitat with fence/hide/zebra/wildebeest/impala. The dedicated demonstration of the "4 fenced habitats" headline feature does not show one. Same per-seed camera-anchor idiom as savannah, where an analogous (less severe) mismatch was found independently this round -- likely a systemic weakness, not two unrelated one-offs.

close preset shows a wide establishing view, not the promised lodge-veranda close-up with visible pool -- the lodge assets exist (confirmed in lodge/night presets) but this preset's camera does not frame them as described.
tour preset's safari truck not visually confirmed -- kopje subject correct but no vehicle located in frame.
Waterhole/pan surfaces read anomalously bright at night -- same bug independently confirmed in five other modules this round (terrain, animals, traffic, savannah); not park's own code.

park.good: gate, lodge, and night all deliver exactly what their descriptions promise with real detailed construction and atmospheric lighting. Whole-park overview (once correctly captured) shows a coherent real composite built through the other modules' own APIs. Zero console errors anywhere; draw calls comfortably within budget. README documents an unusually rigorous numbers-based gameplay-fidelity verification (price elasticity, births, drought/disease/poaching/prosperity) via tools/fidelity.mjs -- not re-run this round, flagged for next pass to verify directly.

issues.text: Night-water-overbright bug is real, severe, and project-wide -- NOT resolved, contrary to round 4's characterization. Independently found and measured (raw pixel readback in terrain's review: water ~2.5-3x brighter than surrounding ground/sky) in six separate contexts this round: terrain, animals, traffic, savannah, park, and now the game's own default overview-21.5 shot and the savannah-subject night shot in this blind pass. Round 4 scored these shots 7.5 describing "dark-water highlights" and "bright moon-glint" -- a fresh independent look finds the water uniformly and severely overexposed, the dominant visual feature of the frame, not a highlight or glint. Single most damaging, most-corroborated defect found in this entire critic pass; affects the game's own default night view.

Camera-anchor mis-targeting in wave-3 composite modules (savannah, park): savannah's close preset shows a herd crossing instead of its promised foreground-grass-and-acacia-trunk-with-hazy-kopje composition (near-duplicate of the herd preset); park's habitat preset shows a river/gallery scene instead of the promised plains-grazer habitat with fence/hide/species, and park's close preset shows a wide establishing view instead of a lodge-veranda close-up. Very likely the same underlying class of defect (not three unrelated one-offs): both modules use the same shared idiom of recomputing camera anchors from real per-seed feature positions at stage() time. Recommend the integrator fix this once as a shared-idiom issue (e.g. a common anchor-validation helper rejecting anchors too close to another preset's subject or habitat) rather than patching each module independently.

Daytime overview/close game shots (8h, 14h) are genuinely strong and stable -- both this round and round 4 agree closely; earlier terrain/props/environment fixes (waterline sparkle, grass mottle, tiled cracks) continue to hold up under a fresh independent look.
Newly-observed minor triangle-budget overage on the close presets (~6.08-6.11M vs the <=6M target); not present at overview (4.7-4.8M). Not previously flagged.
game.gameplayFidelity (8.0) was not re-verified this round -- tools/fidelity.mjs not re-run due to session time budget spent on the full 15-module pass. Flagged for the next round to re-run directly.
